name: Christina Rossetti
credit: Portrait of Christina Rossetti · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Christina Rossetti (1830–1894) was an English poet of devotional intensity and quiet formal mastery, sister of the painter-poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti.
Best known for ‘Goblin Market’ and the carol ‘In the Bleak Midwinter,’ she also wrote Sing-Song (1872), a book of nursery rhymes for children.

poems.title: Angels at the foot
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Angels at the foot,
And Angels at the head,
And like a curly little lamb
My pretty babe in bed.

poems.title: Love me,—I love you
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Love me,—I love you,
Love me, my baby;
Sing it high, sing it low,
Sing it as may be.

poems.title: Mother’s arms under you
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Mother’s arms under you,
Her eyes above you;
Sing it high, sing it low,
Love me,—I love you.

poems.title: My baby has a father and a mother
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
My baby has a father and a mother,
Rich little baby!
Fatherless, motherless, I know another
Forlorn as may be:
Poor little baby!

poems.title: Our little baby fell asleep
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Our little baby fell asleep,
And may not wake again
For days and days, and weeks and weeks
But then he’ll wake again,
And come with his own pretty look,
And kiss Mamma again.

poems.title: Kookoorookoo! kookoorookoo!”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Kookoorookoo! kookoorookoo!”
Crows the cock before the morn
“Kikirikee! kikirikee!”
Roses in the east are born.

poems.title: Kookoorookoo! kookoorookoo!”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Kookoorookoo! kookoorookoo!”
Early birds begin their singing;
“Kikirikee! kikirikee!”
The day, the day, the day is springing.

poems.title: Baby cry—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Baby cry—
Oh fie!—
At the physic in the cup:
Gulp it twice
And gulp it thrice,
Baby gulp it up.

poems.title: Eight o’clock
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Bread and milk for breakfast
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Bread and milk for breakfast,
And woollen frocks to wear,
And a crumb for robin redbreast
On the cold days of the year.

poems.title: There’s snow on the fields
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
There’s snow on the fields,
And cold in the cottage,
While I sit in the chimney nook
Supping hot pottage.

poems.title: My clothes are soft and warm
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
My clothes are soft and warm,
Fold upon fold,
But I’m so sorry for the poor
Out in the cold.

poems.title: Dead in the cold, a song-singing thrush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Dead in the cold, a song-singing thrush,
Dead at the foot of a snowberry bush,—
Weave him a coffin of rush,
Dig him a grave where the soft mosses grow,
Raise him a tombstone of snow.

poems.title: I dug and dug amongst the snow
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I dug and dug amongst the snow,
And thought the flowers would never grow;
I dug and dug amongst the sand,
And still no green thing came to hand.

poems.title: Melt, O snow! the warm winds blow
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Melt, O snow! the warm winds blow
To thaw the flowers and melt the snow
But all the winds from every land
Will rear no blossom from the sand.

poems.title: A city plum is not a plum
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Your brother has a falcon
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Your brother has a falcon,
Your sister has a flower;
But what is left for mannikin,
Born within an hour?

poems.title: I’ll nurse you on my knee, my knee
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I’ll nurse you on my knee, my knee,
My own little son;
I’ll rock you, rock you, in my arms,
My least little one.

poems.title: Hear what the mournful linnets say
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Hear what the mournful linnets say:
“We built our nest compact and warm.
But cruel boys came round our way
And took our summerhouse by storm.

poems.title: They crushed the eggs so neatly laid
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“They crushed the eggs so neatly laid;
So now we sit with drooping wing,
And watch the ruin they have made,
Too late to build, too sad to sing.”

poems.title: A baby’s cradle with no baby in it
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A baby’s cradle with no baby in it,
A baby’s grave where autumn leaves drop sere;
The sweet soul gathered home to Paradise,
The body waiting here.

poems.title: Hop-o’-my-thumb and little Jack Horner
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Hop-o’-my-thumb and little Jack Horner,
What do you mean by tearing and fighting?
Sturdy dog Trot close round the corner,
I never caught him growling and biting.

poems.title: Hope is like a harebell trembling from its birth.
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: O wind, why do you never rest
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
O wind, why do you never rest,
Wandering, whistling to and fro,
Bringing rain out of the west,
From the dim north bringing snow?

poems.title: Crying, my little one, footsore and weary?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Crying, my little one, footsore and weary?
Fall asleep, pretty one, warm on my shoulder:
I must tramp on through the winter night dreary,
While the snow falls on me colder and colder.

poems.title: You are my one, and I have not another
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Growing in the vale
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Growing in the vale
By the uplands hilly,
Growing straight and frail,
Lady Daffadowndilly.

poems.title: In a golden crown
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
In a golden crown,
And a scant green gown
While the spring blows chilly,
Lady Daffadown,
Sweet Daffadowndilly.

poems.title: A linnet in a gilded cage,—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A linnet in a gilded cage,—
A linnet on a bough,—
In frosty winter one might doubt
Which bird is luckier now.

poems.title: But let the trees burst out in leaf
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
But let the trees burst out in leaf,
And nests be on the bough,
Which linnet is the luckier bird,
Oh who could doubt it now?

poems.title: Wrens and robins in the hedge
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Wrens and robins in the hedge,
Wrens and robins here and there;
Building, perching, pecking, fluttering,
Everywhere!

poems.title: My baby has a mottled fist
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
My baby has a mottled fist,
My baby has a neck in creases;
My baby kisses and is kissed,
For he’s the very thing for kisses.

poems.title: Why did baby die
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Why did baby die,
Making Father sigh,
Mother cry?

poems.title: Flowers, that bloom to die
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Flowers, that bloom to die,
Make no reply
Of “why?”
But bow and die.

poems.title: If all were rain and never sun
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If all were rain and never sun,
No bow could span the hill;
If all were sun and never rain,
There’d be no rainbow still.

poems.title: O wind, where have you been
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
O wind, where have you been,
That you blow so sweet?
Among the violets
Which blossom at your feet.

poems.title: The honeysuckle waits
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The honeysuckle waits
For Summer and for heat.
But violets in the chilly Spring
Make the turf so sweet.

poems.title: Brownie, Brownie, let down your milk
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Brownie, Brownie, let down your milk
White as swansdown and smooth as silk,
Fresh as dew and pure as snow:
For I know where the cowslips blow,
And you shall have a cowslip wreath
No sweeter scented than your breath.

poems.title: On the grassy banks
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
On the grassy banks
Lambkins at their pranks;
Woolly sisters, woolly brothers
Jumping off their feet
While their woolly mothers
Watch by them and bleat.

poems.title: Rushes in a watery place
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Minnie and Mattie
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Minnie and Mattie
And fat little May,
Out in the country,
Spending a day.

poems.title: Such a bright day
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Such a bright day,
With the sun glowing,
And the trees half in leaf,
And the grass growing.

poems.title: Pinky white pigling
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Pinky white pigling
Squeals through his snout,
Woolly white lambkin
Frisks all about.

poems.title: Cluck! cluck! the nursing hen
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Cluck! cluck! the nursing hen
Summons her folk,—
Ducklings all downy soft
Yellow as yolk.

poems.title: Cluck! cluck! the mother hen
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Cluck! cluck! the mother hen
Summons her chickens
To peck the dainty bits
Found in her pickings.

poems.title: Minnie and Mattie
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Minnie and Mattie
And May carry posies,
Half of sweet violets,
Half of primroses.

poems.title: Give the sun time enough
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Give the sun time enough,
Glowing and glowing,
He’ll rouse the roses
And bring them blowing.

poems.title: Don’t wait for roses
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Don’t wait for roses
Losing to-day,
O Minnie, Mattie,
And wise little May.

poems.title: Violets and primroses
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Violets and primroses
Blossom to-day
For Minnie and Mattie
And fat little May.

poems.title: Heartsease in my garden bed
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Heartsease in my garden bed,
With sweetwilliam white and red,
Honeysuckle on my wall:—
Heartsease blossoms in my heart
When sweet William comes to call,
But it withers when we part,
And the honey-trumpets fall.

poems.title: If I were a Queen
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If I were a Queen,
What would I do?
I’d make you King,
And I’d wait on you.

poems.title: If I were a King
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If I were a King,
What would I do?
I’d make you Queen,
For I’d marry you.

poems.title: What are heavy? sea-sand and sorrow
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What are heavy? sea-sand and sorrow:
What are brief? to-day and to-morrow:
What are frail? Spring blossoms and youth
What are deep? the ocean and truth.

poems.title: Stroke a flint, and there is nothing to admire
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Stroke a flint, and there is nothing to admire:
Strike a flint, and forthwith flash out sparks of
fire.

poems.title: There is but one May in the year
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
There is but one May in the year,
And sometimes May is wet and cold;
There is but one May in the year
Before the year grows old.

poems.title: Yet though it be the chilliest May
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Yet though it be the chilliest May,
With least of sun and most of showers,
Its wind and dew, its night and day,
Bring up the flowers.

poems.title: The summer nights are short
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The summer nights are short
Where northern days are long:
For hours and hours lark after lark
Trills out his song.

poems.title: The summer days are short
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The summer days are short
Where southern nights are long:
Yet short the night when nightingales
Trill out their song.

poems.title: The days are clear
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The days are clear,
Day after day,
When April’s here,
That leads to May,
And June
Must follow soon:
Stay, June, stay!—
If only we could stop the moon
And June!

poems.title: Twist me a crown of wind-flowers
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Twist me a crown of wind-flowers;
That I may fly away
To hear the singers at their song,
And players at their play.
Put on your crown of wind-flowers
But whither would you go?
Beyond the surging of the sea
And the storms that blow.
Alas! your crown of wind-flowers
Can never make you fly:
I twist them in a crown to-day,
And to-night they die.

poems.title: Brown and furry
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Brown and furry
Caterpillar in a hurry,
Take your walk
To the shady leaf, or stalk,
Or what not,
Which may be the chosen spot.
No toad spy you,
Hovering bird of prey pass by you
Spin and die,
To live again a butterfly.

poems.title: A toadstool comes up in a night,—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A toadstool comes up in a night,—
Learn the lesson, little folk:—
An oak grows on a hundred years,
But then it is an oak.

poems.title: A pocket handkerchief to hem—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A pocket handkerchief to hem—
On dear, oh dear, oh dear!
How many stitches it will take
Before it’s done, I fear.

poems.title: Yet set a stitch and then a stitch
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Yet set a stitch and then a stitch,
And stitch and stitch away,
Till stitch by stitch the hem is done—
And after work is play!

poems.title: If a pig wore a wig
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If a pig wore a wig,
What could we say?
Treat him as a gentleman,
And say “Good day.”
If his tail chanced to fail,
What could we do?—
Send him to the tailoress
To get one new.

poems.title: Seldom “can’t,”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Seldom “can’t,”
Seldom “don’t”
Never “shan’t,”
Never “won’t.”

poems.title: 1 and 1 are 2
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
1 and 1 are 2
That’s for me and you.

poems.title: 2 and 2 are 4—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
2 and 2 are 4—
That’s a couple more.

poems.title: 3 and 3 are 6
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
3 and 3 are 6
Barley-sugar sticks.

poems.title: 4 and 4 are 8
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
4 and 4 are 8
Tumblers at the gate.

poems.title: 5 and 5 are 10
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
5 and 5 are 10
Bluff seafaring men.

poems.title: 6 and 6 are 12
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
6 and 6 are 12
Garden lads who delve.

poems.title: 7 and 7 are 14
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
7 and 7 are 14
Young men bent on sporting.

poems.title: 8 and 8 are 16
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
8 and 8 are 16
Pills the doctor’s mixing.

poems.title: 9 and 9 are 18
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
9 and 9 are 18
Passengers kept waiting.

poems.title: 10 and 10 are 20
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
10 and 10 are 20
Roses—pleasant plenty!

poems.title: 11 and 11 are 22
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
11 and 11 are 22
Sums for brother George to do.

poems.title: 12 and 12 are 24
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
12 and 12 are 24
Pretty pictures, and no more.

poems.title: How many seconds in a minute?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many seconds in a minute?
Sixty, and no more in it.

poems.title: How many minutes in an hour?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many minutes in an hour?
Sixty for sun and shower.

poems.title: How many hours in a day?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many hours in a day?
Twenty-four for work and play.

poems.title: How many days in a week?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many days in a week?
Seven both to hear and speak.

poems.title: How many weeks in a month?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many weeks in a month?
Four, as the swift moon runn’th.

poems.title: How many months in a year?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many months in a year?
Twelve the almanack makes clear.

poems.title: How many years in an age?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many years in an age?
One hundred says the sage.

poems.title: How many ages in time?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
How many ages in time?
No one knows the rhyme.

poems.title: What will you give me for my pound?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What will you give me for my pound?
Full twenty shillings round.
What will you give me for my shilling?
Twelve pence to give I’m willing.
What will you give me for my penny?
Four farthings, just so many.

poems.title: January cold desolate
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: What is pink? a rose is pink
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What is pink? a rose is pink
By the fountain’s brink.
What is red? a poppy’s red
In its barlev bed.
What is blue? the sky is blue
Where the clouds float thro’.
What is white? a swan is white
Sailing in the light.
What is yellow: pears are yellow,
Rich and ripe and mellow.
What is green? the grass is green.
With small flowers between.
What is violet? clouds are violet
In the summer twilight.
What is orange? why, an orange,
Just an orange!

poems.title: Mother shake the cherry-tree
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Mother shake the cherry-tree,
Susan catch a cherry;
Oh how funny that will be,
Let’s be merry!
One for brother, one for sister,
Two for mother more,
Six for father, hot and tired,
Knocking at the door.

poems.title: A pin has a head, but has no hair
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Hopping frog, hop here and be seen
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Hopping frog, hop here and be seen,
I’ll not pelt you with stick or stone:
Your cap is laced and your coat is green;
Good bye, we’ll let each other alone.

poems.title: Plodding toad, plod here and be looked at
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Plodding toad, plod here and be looked at,
You the finger of scorn is crooked at:
But though you’re lumpish, you’re harmless too;
You won’t hurt me, and I won’t hurt you.

poems.title: Where innocent bright-eyed daisies are
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Where innocent bright-eyed daisies are,
With blades of grass between,
Each daisy stands up like a star
Out of a sky of green.

poems.title: The city mouse Jives in a house;—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The city mouse Jives in a house;—
The garden mouse lives in a bower,
He’s friendly with the frogs and toads,
And sees the pretty plants in flower.

poems.title: The city mouse eats bread and cheese;—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The city mouse eats bread and cheese;—
The garden mouse eats what he can;
We will not grudge him seeds and stalks,
Poor little timid furry man.

poems.title: What does the donkey bray about?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What does the donkey bray about?
What does the pig grunt through his snout?
What does the goose mean by a hiss?
Oh, Nurse, if you can tell me this,
I’ll give you such a kiss.
The cockatoo calls “cockatoo,”
The magpie chatters “how d’ye do?”
The jackdaw bids me “go away,”
Cuckoo cries “cuckoo” half the day:
What do the others say?

poems.title: Three plum buns
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Three plum buns
To eat here at the stile
In the clover meadow,
For we have walked a mile.

poems.title: One for you, and one for me
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
One for you, and one for me,
And one left over:
Give it to the boy who shouts
To scare sheep from the clover.

poems.title: A motherless soft lambkin
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A motherless soft lambkin
Alone upon a hill;
No mother’s fleece to shelter him
And wrap him from the cold:—
I’ll run to him and comfort him,
I’ll fetch him, that I will;
I’ll care for him and feed him
Until he’s strong and bold.

poems.title: Dancing on the hill-tops
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Dancing on the hill-tops,
Singing in the valleys,
Laughing with the echoes,
Merry little Alice.

poems.title: Playing games with lambkins
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Playing games with lambkins
In the flowering valleys,
Gathering pretty posies,
Helpful little Alice.

poems.title: If her father’s cottage
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If her father’s cottage
Turned into a palace,
And he owned the hill-tops
And the flowering valleys,
She’d be none the happier,
Happy little Alice.

poems.title: When fishes set umbrellas up
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
When fishes set umbrellas up
If the rain-drops run,
Lizards will want their parasols
To shade them from the sun.

poems.title: The peacock has a score of eyes
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Pussy has a whiskered face
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Pussy has a whiskered face,
Kitty has such pretty ways;
Doggie scampers when I call,
And has a heart to love us all.

poems.title: The dog lies in his kennel
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The dog lies in his kennel,
And Puss purrs on the rug,
And baby perches on my knee
For me to love and hug.

poems.title: Pat the dog and stroke the cat
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Pat the dog and stroke the cat,
Each in its degree;
And cuddle and kiss my baby,
And baby kiss me.

poems.title: If hope grew on a bush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If hope grew on a bush,
And joy grew on a tree,
What a nosegay for the plucking
There would be!
But oh! in windy autumn,
When frail flowers wither,
What should we do for hope and joy,
Fading together?

poems.title: I planted a hand
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I planted a hand
And there came up a palm,
I planted a heart
And there came up balm.
Then I planted a wish,
But there sprang a thorn,
While heaven frowned with thunder
And earth sighed forlorn.

poems.title: Under the ivy bush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Under the ivy bush
One sits sighing,
And under the willow tree
One sits crying:—

poems.title: Under the ivy bush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Under the ivy bush
Cease from your sighing,
But under the willow tree
Lie down a-dying.

poems.title: I am a King
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I am a King,
Or an Emperor rather,
I wear crown-imperial
And prince’s-feather;
Golden-rod is the sceptre
I wield and wag,
And a broad purple flag-flower
Waves for my flag.

poems.title: Elder the pithy
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Elder the pithy
With old-man and sage,
These are my councillors
Green in old age;
Lords-and-ladies in silence
Stand round me and wait,
While gay ragged-robin
Makes bows at my gate.

poems.title: There is one that has a head without an eye
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
There is one that has a head without an eye,
And there’s one that has an eye without a head:
You may find the answer if you try;
And when all is said,
Half the answer hangs upon a thread!

poems.title: If a mouse could fly
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If a mouse could fly,
Or if a crow could swim,
Or if a sprat could walk and talk,
I’d like to be like him.

poems.title: If a mouse could fly
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Sing me a song—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Sing me a song—
What shall I sing?—
Three merry sisters
Dancing in a ring,
Light and fleet upon their feet
As birds upon the wing.

poems.title: Tell me a tale—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Tell me a tale—
What shall I tell?—
Two mournful sisters,
And a tolling knell,
Tolling ding and tolling dong,
Ding dong bell.

poems.title: The lily has an air
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The lily has an air,
And the snowdrop a grace,
And the sweetpea a way,
And the heartsease a face,—
Yet there’s nothing like the rose
When she blows.

poems.title: Margaret has a milking-pail
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Margaret has a milking-pail,
And she rises early;
Thomas has a threshing-flail,
And he’s up betimes.
Sometimes crossing through the grass
Where the dew lies pearly,
They say “Good morrow” as they pass
By the leafy limes.

poems.title: In the meadow—what in the meadow?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
In the meadow—what in the meadow?
Bluebells, buttercups, meadowsweet,
And fairy rings for the children’s feet
In the meadow.
In the garden—what in the garden?
Jacob’s-ladder and Solomon’s-seal,
And Love-lies-bleeding beside All-heal
In the garden.

poems.title: A frisky lamb
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A frisky lamb
And a frisky child
Playing their pranks
In a cowslip meadow:
The sky all blue
And the air all mild
And the fields all sun
And the lanes half shadow.

poems.title: Mix a pancake
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Mix a pancake,
Stir a pancake,
Pop it in the pan;
Fry the pancake,
Toss the pancake,—
Catch it if you can.

poems.title: The wind has such a rainy sound
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The wind has such a rainy sound
Moaning through the town,
The sea has such a windy sound,—
Will the ships go down?

poems.title: The apples in the orchard
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The apples in the orchard
Tumble from their tree.—
Oh, will the ships go down, go down,
In the windy sea?

poems.title: Three little children
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Three little children
On the wide wide earth,
Motherless children—
Cared for from their birth
By tender angels.

poems.title: Three little children
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Three little children
On the wide wide sea,
Motherless children—
Safe as safe can be
With guardian angels.

poems.title: Fly away, fly away over the sea
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Fly away, fly away over the sea,
Sun-loving swallow, for summer is done;
Come again, come again, come back to me,
Bringing the summer and bringing the sun.

poems.title: Minnie bakes oaten cakes
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Minnie bakes oaten cakes,
Minnie brews ale,
All because her Johnny’s coming
Home from sea.
And she glows like a rose,
Who was so pale,
And “Are you sure the church clock goes?”
Says she.

poems.title: A white hen sitting
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A white hen sitting
On white eggs three:
Next, three speckled chickens
As plump as plump can be.

poems.title: An owl, and a hawk
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
An owl, and a hawk,
And a bat come to see:
But chicks beneath their mother’s wing
Squat safe as safe can be.

poems.title: Currants on a bush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Currants on a bush,
And figs upon a stem,
And cherries on a bending bough,
And Ned to gather them.

poems.title: Playing at bob cherry
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Playing at bob cherry
Tom and Nell and Hugh:
Cherry bob! cherry bob!
There’s a bob for you.

poems.title: Tom bobs a cherry
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Tom bobs a cherry
For gaping snapping Hugh,
While curly-pated Nelly
Snaps at it too.

poems.title: Look, look, look—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Look, look, look—
Oh what a sight to see!
The wind is playing cherry bob
With the cherry tree.

poems.title: I have but one rose in the world
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I have but one rose in the world,
And my one rose stands a-drooping:
Oh, when my single rose is dead
There’ll be but thorns for stooping.

poems.title: Rosy maiden Winifred
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Rosy maiden Winifred,
With a milkpail on her head,
Tripping through the corn,
While the dew lies on the wheat
In the sunny morn.
Scarlet shepherd’s-weatherglass
Spreads wide open at her feet
As they pass;
Cornflowers give their almond smell
While she brushes by,
And a lark sings from the sky
“All is well.”

poems.title: Blind from my birth
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Blind from my birth,
Where flowers are springing
I sit on earth
All dark.
Hark! hark!
A lark is singing,
His notes are all for me,
For me his mirth:—
Till some day I shall see
Beautiful flowers
And birds in bowers
Where all Joy Bells are ringing.

poems.title: When the cows come home the milk is coming
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Roses blushing red and white
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Ding a ding,”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Ding a ding,”
The sweet bells sing,
And say:
“Come, all be gay”
For a wedding day.

poems.title: Dong a dong,”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Dong a dong,”
The bells sigh long,
And call:
“Weep one, weep all”
For a funeral.

poems.title: A ring upon her finger
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A ring upon her finger,
Walks the bride,
With the bridegroom tall and handsome
At her side.

poems.title: A veil upon her forehead
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A veil upon her forehead,
Walks the bride,
With the bridegroom proud and merry
At her side.

poems.title: Fling flowers beneath the footsteps
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Fling flowers beneath the footsteps
Of the bride;
Fling flowers before the bridegroom
At her side.

poems.title: Ferry me across the water
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Ferry me across the water,
Do, boatman, do.”
“If you’ve a penny in your purse
I’ll ferry you.”

poems.title: I have a penny in my purse
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“I have a penny in my purse,
And my eyes are blue;
So ferry me across the water,
Do, boatman, do.”

poems.title: Step into my ferry-boat
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Step into my ferry-boat,
Be they black or blue,
And for the penny in your purse
I’ll ferry you.”

poems.title: When a mounting skylark sings
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
When a mounting skylark sings
In the sunlit summer morn,
I know that heaven is up on high.
And on earth are fields of corn.

poems.title: But when a nightingale sings
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
But when a nightingale sings
In the moonlit summer even,
I know not if earth is merely earth.
Only that heaven is heaven.

poems.title: Who has seen the wind?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Who has seen the wind?
Neither I nor you:
But when the leaves hang trembling
The wind is passing thro’.

poems.title: Who has seen the wind?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Who has seen the wind?
Neither you nor I:
But when the trees bow down their heads
The wind is passing by.

poems.title: The horses of the sea
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The horses of the sea
Rear a foaming crest,
But the horses of the land
Serve us the best.

poems.title: The horses of the land
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The horses of the land
Munch corn and clover,
While the foaming sea-horses
Toss and turn over.

poems.title: O sailor, come ashore
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
O sailor, come ashore,
What have you brought for me?
Red coral, white coral,
Coral from the sea.

poems.title: I did not dig it from the ground
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I did not dig it from the ground,
Nor pluck it from a tree;
Feeble insects made it
In the stormy sea.

poems.title: A diamond or a coal?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A diamond or a coal?
A diamond, if you please:
Who cares about a clumsy coal
Beneath the summer trees?

poems.title: A diamond or a coal?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A diamond or a coal?
A coal, sir, if you please:
One comes to care about the coal
What time the waters freeze.

poems.title: An emerald is as green as grass
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: A diamond is a brilliant stone
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Boats sail on the rivers
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Boats sail on the rivers,
And ships sail on the seas;
But clouds that sail across the sky
Are prettier far than these.

poems.title: There are bridges on the rivers
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
There are bridges on the rivers,
As pretty as you please;
But the bow that bridges heaven,
And overtops the trees,
And builds a road from earth to sky,
Is prettier far than these.

poems.title: The lily has a smooth stalk
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The lily has a smooth stalk,
Will never hurt your hand;
But the rose upon her briar
Is lady of the land.

poems.title: There’s sweetness in an apple tree
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
There’s sweetness in an apple tree,
And profit in the corn;
But lady of all beauty
Is a rose upon a thorn.

poems.title: When with moss and honey
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
When with moss and honey
She tips her bending briar,
And half unfolds her glowing heart,
She sets the world on fire.

poems.title: Hurt no living thing
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Hurt no living thing:
Ladybird, nor butterfly,
Nor moth with dusty wing,
Nor cricket chirping cheerily,
Nor grasshopper so light of leap,
Nor dancing gnat, nor beetle fat,
Nor harmless worms that creep.

poems.title: I caught a little ladybird
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I caught a little ladybird
That flies far away;
I caught a little lady wife
That is both staid and gay.

poems.title: Come back, my scarlet ladybird
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Come back, my scarlet ladybird,
Back from far away;
I weary of my dolly wife,
My wife that cannot play.

poems.title: She’s such a senseless wooden thing
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
She’s such a senseless wooden thing
She stares the livelong day;
Her wig of gold is stiff and cold
And cannot change to grey.

poems.title: All the bells were ringing
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
All the bells were ringing
And all the birds were singing,
When Molly sat down crying
For her broken doll:
O you silly Moll!
Sobbing and sighing
For a broken doll,
When all the bells are ringing,
And all the birds are singing.

poems.title: Wee wee husband
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Wee wee husband,
Give me some money,
I have no comfits,
And I have no honey.

poems.title: Wee wee wifie
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Wee wee wifie,
I have no money,
Milk, nor meat, nor bread to eat,
Comfits, nor honey.

poems.title: I have a little husband
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I have a little husband
And he is gone to sea,
The winds that whistle round his ship
Fly home to me.

poems.title: The winds that sigh about me
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The winds that sigh about me
Return again to him;
So I would fly, if only I
Were light of limb.

poems.title: The dear old woman in the lane
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The dear old woman in the lane
Is sick and sore with pains and aches,
We’ll go to her this afternoon,
And take her tea and eggs and cakes.

poems.title: We’ll stop to make the kettle boil
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
We’ll stop to make the kettle boil,
And brew some tea, and set the tray,
And poach an egg, and toast a cake,
And wheel her chair round, if we may.

poems.title: Swift and sure the swallow
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Swift and sure the swallow,
Slow and sure the snail:
Slow and sure may miss his way,
Swift and sure may fail.

poems.title: I dreamt I caught a little owl
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“I dreamt I caught a little owl
And the bird was blue—”

poems.title: But you may hunt for ever
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“But you may hunt for ever
And not find such an one.”

poems.title: I dreamt I set a sunflower
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“I dreamt I set a sunflower,
And red as blood it grew—”

poems.title: But such a sunflower never
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“But such a sunflower never
Bloomed beneath the sun.”

poems.title: What does the bee do?
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What does the bee do?
Bring home honey.
And what does Father do?
Bring home money.
And what does Mother do?
Lay out the money.
And what does baby do?
Eat up the honey.

poems.title: I have a Poll parrot
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I have a Poll parrot,
And Poll is my doll,
And my nurse is Polly,
And my sister Poll.

poems.title: Polly!” cried Polly
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Polly!” cried Polly,
“Don’t tear Polly dolly”—
While soft-hearted Poll
Trembled for the doll.

poems.title: A house of cards
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A house of cards
Is neat and small
Shake the table,
It must fall.

poems.title: Find the Court cards
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Find the Court cards
One by one;
Raise it, roof it,—
Now it’s done:—
Shake the table!
That’s the fun.

poems.title: The rose with such a bonny blush
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The rose with such a bonny blush,
What has the rose to blush about?
If it’s the sun that makes her flush,
What’s in the sun to flush about?

poems.title: The rose that blushes rosy red
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The rose that blushes rosy red,
She must hang her head;
The lily that blows spotless white,
She may stand upright.

poems.title: Oh, fair to see
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Oh, fair to see
Bloom-laden cherry tree,
Arrayed in sunny white;
An April day’s delight,
Oh, fair to see!

poems.title: Oh, fair to see
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Oh, fair to see
Fruit-laden cherry tree,
With balls of shining red
Decking a leafy head,
Oh, fair to see!

poems.title: Clever little Willie wee
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Clever little Willie wee,
Bright-eyed, blue-eyed little fellow;
Merry little Margery
With her hair all yellow.

poems.title: Little Willie in his heart
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Little Willie in his heart
Is a sailor on the sea,
And he often cons a chart
With sister Margery.

poems.title: The peach tree on the southern wall
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
The peach tree on the southern wall
Has basked so long beneath the sun,
Her score of peaches great and small
Bloom rosy, every one.

poems.title: A peach for brothers, one for each
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
A peach for brothers, one for each,
A peach for you and a peach for me;
But the biggest, rosiest, downiest peach
For Grandmamma with her tea.

poems.title: A rose has thorns as well as honey
poems.author: Christina Rossetti

poems.title: Is the moon tired? she looks so pale
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Is the moon tired? she looks so pale
Within her misty veil:
She scales the sky from east to west,
And takes no rest.

poems.title: Before the coming of the night
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Before the coming of the night
The moon shows papery white;
Before the dawning of the day
She fades away.

poems.title: If stars dropped out of heaven
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If stars dropped out of heaven,
And if flowers took their place,
The sky would still look very fair,
And fair earth’s face.

poems.title: Winged angels might fly down to us
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Winged angels might fly down to us
To pluck the stars,
But we could only long for flowers
Beyond the cloudy bars.

poems.title: Goodbye in fear, goodbye in sorrow
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Goodbye in fear, goodbye in sorrow,
Goodbye, and all in vain,
Never to meet again, my dear—”
“Never to part again.”
“Goodbye to-day, goodbye to-morrow,
Goodbye till earth shall wane,
Never to meet again, my dear—”
“Never to part again.”

poems.title: If the sun could tell us half
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If the sun could tell us half
That he hears and sees,
Sometimes he would make us laugh,
Sometimes make us cry:
Think of all the birds that make
Homes among the trees;
Think of cruel boys who take
Birds that cannot fly.

poems.title: If the moon came from heaven
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
If the moon came from heaven,
Talking all the way,
What could she have to tell us,
And what could she say?

poems.title: I’ve seen a hundred pretty things
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“I’ve seen a hundred pretty things,
And seen a hundred gay
But only think: I peep by night
And do not peep by day!”

poems.title: O Lady Moon, your horns point toward the east
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
O Lady Moon, your horns point toward the east:
Shine, be increased;
O Lady Moon, your horns point toward the west:
Wane, be at rest.

poems.title: What do the stars do
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
What do the stars do
Up in the sky,
Higher than the wind can blow,
Or the clouds can fly?

poems.title: Each star in its own glory
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Each star in its own glory
Circles, circles still;
As it was lit to shine and set,
And do its Maker’s will.

poems.title: Motherless baby and babyless mother
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Motherless baby and babyless mother,
Bring them together to love one another.

poems.title: Crimson curtains round my mother’s bed
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Crimson curtains round my mother’s bed,
Silken soft as may be;
Cool white curtains round about my bed,
For I am but a baby.

poems.title: Baby lies so fast asleep
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Baby lies so fast asleep
That we cannot wake her:
Will the Angels clad in white
Fly from heaven to take her?

poems.title: Baby lies so fast asleep
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Baby lies so fast asleep
That no pain can grieve her
Put a snowdrop in her hand,
Kiss her once and leave her.

poems.title: I know a baby, such a baby,—
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
I know a baby, such a baby,—
Round blue eyes and cheeks of pink,
Such an elbow furrowed with dimples,
Such a wrist where creases sink.

poems.title: Cuddle and love me, cuddle and love me,”
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
“Cuddle and love me, cuddle and love me,”
Crows the mouth of coral pink:
Oh, the bald head, and, oh, the sweet lips,
And, oh, the sleepy eyes that wink!

poems.title: Lullaby, oh, lullaby!
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Lullaby, oh, lullaby!
Flowers are closed and lambs are sleeping;
Lullaby, oh, lullaby!
Stars are up, the moon is peeping;
Lullaby, oh, lullaby
While the birds are silence keeping,
(Lullaby, oh, lullaby!)
Sleep, my baby, fall a-sleeping,
Lullaby, oh, lullaby!

poems.title: Lie a-bed
poems.author: Christina Rossetti
poems.text:
Lie a-bed,
Sleepy head,
Shut up eyes, bo-peep;
Till daybreak
Never wake:—
Baby, sleep.
